items.note: The model's general plate: value V against project area A, with an in-art title reading 'Valuation of land versus area of the land, with positive initial ecosystem'. Three strokes under an upper-left legend keyed K>0, K=0 and K<0, a dashed rule at V = 0, and three callout boxes along the right edge printing '+E(A) +I(A) : improvement', '+E(A) +0 : do no harm' and '+E(A) -I(A) : pollution'. The abscissa runs 0 to 30 in steps of 5 and the ordinate -30 to 50 in steps of 10, and NEITHER AXIS CARRIES A UNIT: what the 30 areas are - km2, hectares, projects - is given nowhere on the plate or in the section, and the reader learns from the case sections three pages later that the eventual scale is km2 in the thousands. TWO KEYS COMPETE FOR THE SAME THREE STROKES: the legend assigns K signs to the strokes while the callout boxes assign I(A) signs to the same three, and nothing says whether the K>0 curve is the improvement curve or a different curve that happens to rise, so a reader who follows the legend and a reader who follows the boxes will read the same stroke as two different cases. The K<0 crossing of the zero rule near A = 9 IS UNMARKED, and it is the number the paper's whole argument turns on - the area at which a polluting project stops destroying value - while the two callouts that do get coordinates are placed on the other two curves. NO SENTENCE IN THE BODY NAMES THIS FIGURE: the section prints the caption and moves straight into the negative case.

Where Figure 1's three strokes rise, these fall, which is the intended mirror; the zero crossings are again unmarked and again the quantity the section discusses. items.note: The cost-benefit curve for the greening project: abscissa 0 to 14000 in steps of 2000, ordinate -2000 to 4000, one smooth stroke that rises from below zero, peaks and slides back to zero. THE PLATE CARRIES THREE SOFTWARE CALLOUT BOXES WITH FULL SOLVER PRECISION - (4284.776, 0), (5980.428, 1771.08) and (12399.999, 0) - which are the coordinates of a numeric root search handed straight to the typesetter: the two zeros print to three decimals and the maximum to two, the first zero sits one ten-thousandth away from a round 4285, and 12399.999 is 0.001 short of 14000's neighbour. That is a solver artefact masquerading as measurement, in a paper whose underlying model is analytic. THE PROSE ROUNDS THE SAME NUMBERS AND CALLS THEM A RESULT: it says the project loses money 'before the area of project expands to 4285 km2' and reaches 'the maximum gains at 5980 km2', matching the first two boxes, but it NEVER MENTIONS THE SECOND ZERO CROSSING AT 12400 - the point where the project's value returns to nothing, i.e. the upper limit of viable area, and the one number on the plate that constrains the conclusion. The minimum near (2400, -2000) is unlabelled. No axis title, no unit on either axis, no legend, grid only.

items.note: Two raster heatmap panels side by side, headed 'Before Livestock' and 'After Livestock', a projected-metre coordinate frame and black open-circle point symbols laid over pale pink to dark green cells. THE TWO PANELS SHARE THE SAME EXTENT - x ticks 330000, 332000, 334000 and y ticks 3435000, 3437000, 3439000 on both - so the pair is genuinely comparable, which is more than most plates in this census manage. What the comparison means is drawn badly: THE COLOUR RAMPS ARE DUPLICATED RATHER THAN SHARED, one 0-to-1 bar inside each panel, and NEITHER BAR IS NAMED - the reader is not told whether the ramp is a probability of presence, a habitat index or a density, nor what 0 and 1 mean; the near-zero cells are pale pink and are barely distinguishable from the white page, so the low end of the quantity is effectively invisible; no axis carries a title or a CRS, so the numbers are plainly metres but a reader cannot say of what projection; and there is no scale bar and no north arrow on a map exhibit. The POINT LAYERS ARE UNLABELLED: no key says whether a circle is a panda record, a camera trap or a survey site, no count accompanies either panel, yet the left panel visibly carries more circles through the central corridor than the right - the plate's whole finding - and the figure does not annotate it. The green linear feature is likewise unkeyed. CITED BY THE WRONG NUMBER: the only mention near this plate reads 'May(Figure 3)', which sends a reader to the two Kubuqi satellite frames on p9; the caption is the paper's own and truncates at 'before' - the words 'and after livestock application (Liu, 2017)' continue in a line the extractor reads as the next caption.

note:
Paper 181, Team 1902054: the economic cost of land-use projects for problem E 2019. A value model that
adds an ecological term to an intervention term, V(A) = E(A) + I(A), then three worked cases - Kubuqi
desert greening, a Baowu steel plant and the Wolong panda reserve - with a discussion that recommends
reusing degraded land and protecting natural landform. Seventeen pages, ten measured regions over nine
of them, resolving into TEN FIGURE ROWS, no tables, no exclusions and nothing unaccounted.

THE CENSUS IS SMALL AND MOSTLY UNDRESSED. Six of the ten plates are line charts, and the paper draws all
six in the same bare style: grid, strokes, tick numbers, and nothing else. Figures 8 and 10 carry no axis
title, no unit, no legend and no annotation at all, so their curves are identified only by their
captions. Figures 4 and 5 print the numbers the case sections quote but strip their units. The two
valuation plates at the front carry in-art titles and callout boxes, and thereby expose a worse problem:
they are the paper's model drawn twice, and the second drawing changes the sign convention without
saying so - '+E(A)' on Figure 1's boxes becomes '-V(A)' on Figure 2's - and changes the ordinate from
-30-to-50 to -50-to-50, so the two halves of one statement cannot be laid over each other.

THE ARITHMETIC IS THE PAPER'S STRONGEST FEATURE AND ITS LEAST EXAMINED. Figure 4's two callouts, "Value
turns positive at 2091" and "Value reaches maximum at 4500", reproduce the citing sentence's 2091 km2 and
4500 km2 exactly. Figure 5's boxes reproduce the prose's 4285 and 5980. That agreement is real, and it
is also the only check the paper ever performs: the same Figure 5 boxes print a third coordinate,
12399.999, which is the area at which the project's value returns to zero - the upper bound of viability
- and the prose never mentions it. No table exists anywhere in the paper, so nothing else in it can be
checked at all: the coefficients behind the three cases are asserted in prose with no grid, no
sensitivity, and no calibration shown.

THE THREE NON-CHARTS. Figure 3 is the paper's only real evidence - two satellite frames of Kubuqi in
2000 and 2016 - and it is pasted, with sub-captions underneath and no scale bar, no north arrow, no
source and no common landmark, so the reader cannot separate greening from two scenes covering different
ground. Figure 7 is a photograph of a smoking stack captioned "Air pollution in Shanghui", a misspelling
in a section about Baowu Steel, carrying no data, no date, no location and no source, named by no
sentence. Figure 9 is the paper's one map: two projected-metre heatmap panels headed "Before Livestock"
and "After Livestock" over the same extent, which makes the pair genuinely comparable, undermined by two
duplicated unnamed 0-to-1 colour ramps, invisible near-zero cells, unlabelled point layers, no CRS, no
scale bar and no north arrow. Its own finding - fewer panda points in the central corridor after
livestock - is visible in the pixels and annotated nowhere.

CITATION IS CASUAL THROUGHOUT. Only four of the ten plates are named by a sentence, and one of those
four is wrong: p14 sends the reader to "Figure 3" while discussing the panda map that sits on the same
page as Figure 9. Figures 1 and 2 - the model itself - are printed with no prose reference at all, and
Figure 6 is reached by "we can use the following graph". Figure 10 is reached by its own caption's tail.

Families: line 6 (Figures 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10), photo-or-raster-image 2 (Figures 3, 7),
bar 1 (Figure 6), map-or-plan-view 1 (Figure 9).
rules: Measure first, then read the pixels: ten measured regions over nine of seventeen pages resolve into ten figure rows, no tables and no exclusions, because every region this paper measures is an exhibit [place.doc_order].

Two plates presented as one statement are drawn on two scales: Figure 1's ordinate runs -30 to 50 and Figure 2's runs -50 to 50, while the ecological term is written '+E(A)' in the first plate's callouts and '-V(A)' in the second's [geometry.family].
Six of ten rows are named by no sentence: Figures 1, 2, 3, 6, 7 and 10 are reached only through their captions, and Figure 6 by the deictic 'we can use the following graph' [mention.count].

A figure can be cited under the wrong number inside its own section: p14 reads the panda distribution map as 'May(Figure 3)', which is the Kubuqi satellite pair three pages earlier [mention.lead_sentence].

Software output can be typeset as a result: Figure 5 prints three callout boxes reading (4284.776, 0), (5980.428, 1771.08) and (12399.999, 0), i.e. a numeric root search's coordinates to three decimals, while the prose beside it rounds them to 4285 and 5980 and never mentions the second zero crossing at 12400 [caption.verbatim].

No axis anywhere in the paper carries a unit: the two valuation plates have no unit on either axis, Figure 4 prints '2091' and '4500' without the km2 its citing sentence supplies, and Figures 5, 8 and 10 print tick numbers only [geometry.legend].

A stacked plot can fail to compose: Figure 6's four-entry legend mixes a net change with its own components, no bar carries a number, and read off the grid the After column's parts total about 2700 against a Net bar of about 2100 [geometry.family].

A map can be drawn without the apparatus of a map: Figure 9 carries no axis titles, no stated CRS, no scale bar, no north arrow, no source, two duplicated unnamed 0-to-1 colour ramps and unlabelled point layers [geometry.legend].

A photograph can stand where evidence is expected: Figure 7 is a smokestack photograph with no data, date, source or location, captioned with a misspelt city name and named by no sentence [caption.verbatim].
Region order is reading order here, unlike the preceding papers: on p11 the Figure 5 curve occupies region 1 above its Figure 6 columns in region 2 [place.page_order].
